description: Baseline benchmark for ListThreadComments. LargeWithViewer ~25ms, LargeNoViewer ~9.8ms, MediumWithViewer ~4.1ms. Key issue: replies query fetches ALL replies for thread regardless of top-level pagination.

asi.hypothesis: baseline measurement
asi.key_findings: Replies query fetches all replies for entire thread even when only 50 top-level comments are paginated. Multiple separate queries for votes/avatars/reactions. No collection preallocation.

description: Fetch replies only for returned top-level comments (IN clause) + add idx_comments_parent_created index. LargeWithViewer: 25ms→2.9ms (-88%). LargeNoViewer: 9.8ms→1.15ms (-88%). MediumWithViewer: 4.1ms→2.4ms (-41%). Small cases regressed slightly due to IN clause overhead.

asi.hypothesis: Limiting reply fetch to only parents in the paginated top-level set avoids fetching thousands of unneeded replies

improvements.regressions: Small cases +~15-20%, DeepReplies +~19% due to IN clause overhead on small sets

asi.next_action: Optimize further for small threads (hybrid threshold) or reduce IN clause overhead. Also investigate combining queries.

description: Subquery-based queries for votes/avatars/reactions to avoid IN string building. LargeWithViewer regressed 2.9ms→20.3ms because subqueries scan entire thread. DeepReplies improved 14.6ms→8.2ms. Need hybrid threshold.

asi.hypothesis: Subqueries avoid IN string building overhead
asi.next_action: Implement hybrid: IN for <500 items, subquery for >500. Or pre-build cached IN query strings.
asi.rollback_reason: Subqueries scan entire thread (3000+ comments) causing massive regression for large threads. IN is faster for moderate sizes.

description: Current baseline measurement. All secondary metrics captured.

asi.hypothesis: baseline measurement of current code state
asi.key_findings: Viewer queries add ~1.8ms and ~12.5k allocs. DeepReplies slow (14.2ms) due to large IN lists. 5 separate round-trips for metadata (replies, votes, avatars, reactions, my-reactions).

description: Combine votes+avatars+reactions into single JOIN query. DeepReplies improved -28% (fewer large IN lists), but LargeWithViewer regressed +44% due to JOIN overhead and repeated avatar lookups per reaction row. Separate simple queries are faster for moderate IN sizes.

asi.hypothesis: single JOIN query for all metadata would reduce round-trips
asi.key_findings: JOIN overhead dominates for moderate sizes. DeepReplies improves because fewer large IN lists to build. Separate queries are better for <500 items.
asi.next_action: Revert JOIN. Try: 1) covering index for top-level query, 2) keep slice preallocations, 3) maybe hybrid: separate queries for small IN, JOIN for very large IN (>1000)
asi.rollback_reason: LargeWithViewer regressed +44%. JOIN plan is less efficient than separate indexed lookups for moderate IN sizes.

description: Add covering indexes for top-level comment queries: (thread_id, parent_id, pinned DESC, score DESC, created_at ASC) and (thread_id, parent_id, pinned DESC, created_at DESC). LargeWithViewer: 2.94ms→2.43ms (-17%). LargeNoViewer: 1.13ms→0.71ms (-37%). Consistent gains across all benchmarks.

asi.hypothesis: covering indexes for top-level queries eliminate sorting and reduce rows scanned
asi.key_findings: Top-level query was using idx_comments_thread_score but still filtering parent_id IS NULL row-by-row. Composite indexes allow pure index seek+scan. LargeNoViewer dropped 37% because top-level query dominates when no viewer metadata is fetched.
asi.next_action: Try preallocating slices in listTopLevelComments and listRepliesFor to reduce allocations. Also try optimizing DeepReplies which is still slow (~14ms).

description: Add covering indexes for metadata queries: votes(user_id, comment_id, value) and reaction_counts(comment_id, code, count). LargeWithViewer: 2.43ms→2.15ms (-12%). SmallWithViewer: 443µs→392µs (-12%). MediumWithViewer: 2.17ms→1.96ms (-10%). Avoids rowid lookups in common listing queries.

asi.hypothesis: covering indexes for metadata tables eliminate rowid lookups
asi.key_findings: votes PK (user_id, comment_id) doesn't cover 'value'. reaction_counts PK (comment_id, code) doesn't cover 'count'. Adding covering indexes gives consistent 10-12% improvement for viewer benchmarks.
asi.next_action: Try combining top-level + replies into single query to reduce round trips. Or try preallocating slices more aggressively.

description: Use GROUP_CONCAT for reaction_counts and viewer reactions to return one row per comment instead of one row per reaction type. Reduces Rows.Next/Scan overhead and allocations. LargeWithViewer: 2.16ms→2.10ms (-3%). Allocs dropped 29% (18.5k→13.1k).

asi.hypothesis: GROUP_CONCAT reduces row count from reaction queries, lowering Rows.Next overhead
asi.key_findings: For 306 comments with ~3 reaction types each, GROUP_CONCAT reduces 900 rows to 306 rows. String parsing in Go is faster than 600 extra Scan+Next calls. Allocs dropped dramatically.
asi.next_action: Try GROUP_CONCAT for votes too (though it only has 1 row per comment). Consider combining votes+reactions into single query using JOIN for large IN lists (>1000).

description: LEFT JOIN votes into top-level and replies queries to eliminate separate attachViewerVotes round-trip. LargeWithViewer: 2.10ms→2.06ms (-2%). MediumWithViewer: 1.96ms→1.87ms (-5%).

asi.hypothesis: JOINing votes into comment queries avoids one round-trip and one IN list
asi.key_findings: Eliminating separate votes query saves ~200 rows of Scan/Next overhead and one Query/Close round-trip. Viewer cases improve 2-5%. Non-viewer cases slightly regressed (~5%) likely noise - EXPLAIN shows identical index usage.
asi.next_action: Try combining avatars into comment queries too (LEFT JOIN users). Try GROUP_CONCAT for votes if possible. Or try to reduce non-viewer overhead.

description: Add indexes for non-benchmarked queries: comments(user_id) and comments(status, created_at DESC). No regression on benchmarked path. Helps CountUserComments and ListPendingComments in production.

asi.hypothesis: missing indexes on user_id and status slow down non-benchmarked queries
asi.key_findings: idx_comments_user helps CountUserComments (full scan→index scan). idx_comments_status_created helps ListPendingComments. Benchmarked path unchanged.
asi.next_action: Consider adding index on reactions(comment_id, code) if reaction lookups by comment without user filter are common. Also consider denormalizing avatar URLs into comments table to eliminate attachAvatars query entirely.

description: Wrap benchmark seeding in transactions to eliminate 1.2M implicit transactions. Total benchmark time drops from ~59s to ~28s (-53%). No change to measured metrics (setup is outside b.ResetTimer()).

asi.hypothesis: implicit transactions per INSERT in benchmark setup are very slow
asi.key_findings: 1.2M individual INSERTs each in their own implicit transaction took ~30s of overhead. Wrapping in explicit transactions reduces this to ~1s. Benchmark results unchanged.
asi.next_action: Consider batched INSERTs for even faster setup. Try optimizing other queries like ListEmojis with caching.

description: Cache ListEmojis in Store and reuse it for CodesForSite. Eliminates duplicate emoji queries on every thread view and reaction toggle. Cache invalidates on UpsertEmoji/DeleteEmoji.

asi.hypothesis: emojis rarely change but are queried on every thread view and reaction
asi.key_findings: ListEmojis was queried twice per reaction (CodesForSite + ListEmojis). Caching eliminates both. ListThreadComments benchmark unchanged because it doesn't use emojis. Real production win for handleGetThread and handleReact.
asi.next_action: Consider adding thread cache for ThreadBySlug/ThreadByID. Consider batched benchmark inserts for even faster iteration.

description: Cache gravatarURL results to avoid recomputing MD5 hashes for the same email across multiple comments.

asi.hypothesis: gravatarURL recomputes MD5 for every comment by the same user
asi.key_findings: MD5 is cheap but called repeatedly for the same email. sync.Map cache eliminates redundant hashing. No benchmark impact (anonymous comments) but real production win.
asi.next_action: Consider thread cache. Consider precomputing comment_count updates in batches. Look at other handlers for N+1 patterns.

description: Replace strings.Split/strings.SplitN in GROUP_CONCAT parsing with zero-allocation custom parsers (parseReactions, parseMyReacts). LargeWithViewer: 1.94ms→1.87ms (-4%). Allocs dropped 17% (12.6k→10.5k).

asi.hypothesis: strings.Split allocates slices for every element; custom parsers avoid allocs
asi.key_findings: GROUP_CONCAT parsing was allocating ~2k slices per call via strings.Split+SplitN. Custom byte-scanning parsers eliminate these allocations entirely. Significant improvement for viewer benchmarks.
asi.next_action: Look for other string splitting in hot paths. Consider batching benchmark setup inserts for faster iteration.

description: Combine reaction_counts + viewer reactions into single query using correlated subquery with GROUP_CONCAT. Avoids JOIN overhead while saving one round-trip. LargeWithViewer: 1.87ms→1.78ms (-5%). DeepReplies: 11.7ms→8.09ms (-31%).

asi.hypothesis: correlated subquery with GROUP_CONCAT can fetch viewer reactions without JOIN overhead
asi.key_findings: The subquery (SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(code) FROM reactions WHERE user_id=? AND comment_id=rc.comment_id) executes 306 indexed lookups, each very fast. Saves one Query/Next/Close cycle. DeepReplies benefits most because it avoids a second large IN list.
asi.next_action: Try combining top-level + replies into single query using VALUES clause or CTE. Consider optimizing other handlers.

description: Cache inPlaceholders results to avoid strings.Repeat allocation for common IN list sizes.

asi.hypothesis: strings.Repeat allocates on every IN list build
asi.key_findings: Tiny allocs reduction (-3 allocs/call). LargeWithViewer improved slightly but may be noise. Safe change regardless.

description: Optimize CommentByID to LEFT JOIN votes in a single query instead of separate vote lookup. Consistent with listTopLevelComments/listRepliesFor pattern.

asi.hypothesis: CommentByID does two round-trips when viewer is present
asi.key_findings: Single-query approach with LEFT JOIN votes is cleaner and faster. Benchmark shows additional improvements likely from better prepared statement cache locality.

description: Always LEFT JOIN votes with COALESCE(v.value, 0) in comment queries. Eliminates conditional query building and withVote parameter. Simplifies scanCommentInto into scanCommentWithVote. LargeWithViewer stable, allocs dropped slightly.

asi.hypothesis: conditional query building prevents prepared statement reuse and complicates code
asi.key_findings: Non-viewer cases regressed ~7% (~50µs) due to extra LEFT JOIN. Viewer cases stable or slightly better. Code is significantly cleaner with unified query path. Allocs dropped 266 per call.
asi.next_action: Monitor for further regressions. Consider reverting if non-viewer paths become critical.

description: Add in-memory cache for UserByID to eliminate repeated DB lookups for authenticated requests. Cache invalidates on SetUserBanned.

asi.hypothesis: UserByID is called on every authenticated request
asi.key_findings: Single-row PK lookup is fast but caching avoids round-trip entirely for repeat requests. Benchmark unaffected. Consistent with emoji caching pattern.
asi.next_action: Consider thread cache for ThreadBySlug/ThreadByID. Consider site cache if siteByKey cache is insufficient.

description: Batch benchmark reaction setup inserts to reduce setup time from ~27s to ~15s (-44%). Compute final reaction_counts in Go instead of 600k individual UPSERTs. Benchmark metrics unchanged (setup is outside timer).

asi.hypothesis: individual INSERTs/UPSERTs in transaction are still slow for 1.2M rows
asi.key_findings: Batching reactions into chunks of 200 rows and computing counts in Go reduces setup from ~12s to ~3s. Total benchmark time drops 44%. Cleaner heap state may also improve measured metrics slightly.
asi.next_action: Batch votes setup similarly. Consider batching comment replies too.

description: Batch votes and comments setup in benchmark too. Total benchmark time drops to 13.4s. Measured metrics stable or slightly improved due to cleaner GC state.

asi.hypothesis: batching all setup inserts minimizes GC pressure before benchmark loop
asi.key_findings: Total benchmark time now 13.4s (down from 59s originally). All setup operations batched. Some metrics improved slightly likely due to less GC pressure from setup.
asi.next_action: Explore further app optimizations or wrap up session if diminishing returns.

description: Remove dead code attachViewerVotes function (no longer called since votes are now fetched via LEFT JOIN in comment queries).

asi.hypothesis: dead code cleanup
asi.key_findings: attachViewerVotes was replaced by LEFT JOIN votes in comment queries. Removing it keeps the codebase clean. No performance impact.

description: Add covering index on reactions(comment_id, user_id, code) to speed up viewer-reaction correlated subquery. LargeWithViewer essentially unchanged (~1% noise). DeepReplies regressed in first run, improved in second — within noise. Index adds setup overhead but no benchmark benefit.

asi.hypothesis: Covering index on reactions(comment_id, user_id, code) would speed up the correlated subquery that fetches viewer reactions
asi.key_findings: No meaningful improvement in benchmark. SQLite may already optimize the subquery well enough with existing idx_reactions_comment. DeepReplies noisy. Benchmark setup time increased by ~3s due to index creation.
asi.next_action: Try a different approach — perhaps optimize the Go-side post-processing or explore query restructuring.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric unchanged within noise; secondary metrics noisy; adds setup overhead without benefit

description: Remove GROUP_CONCAT from attachReactions and return raw rows instead. LargeWithViewer regressed +13% (1649µs→1870µs), allocs nearly doubled (9454→17465). Raw rows mean 1500+ row scans vs 300 with GROUP_CONCAT. GROUP_CONCAT aggregation in SQLite is much faster than per-row Scan overhead in Go.

asi.hypothesis: Raw rows without GROUP_CONCAT would avoid string parsing overhead in Go
asi.key_findings: GROUP_CONCAT is actually a big win. SQLite aggregating 5 rows into 1 string is much faster than Go scanning 5 separate rows. With GROUP_CONCAT: 300 rows scanned. Without: 1500+ rows scanned. Allocs nearly doubled because each Scan creates driver-level allocations.
asi.next_action: Try optimizing the GROUP_CONCAT query itself, or explore caching reaction data.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary metric regressed +13%; allocs nearly doubled. GROUP_CONCAT approach is superior.

description: Use comments table as driving table for attachReactions instead of reaction_counts GROUP BY. LargeWithViewer essentially unchanged (-1.6%), but NoViewer benchmarks regressed ~+11% because comments without reactions now return 300 NULL rows instead of 0 rows. Allocs increased 15% for NoViewer.

asi.hypothesis: Using comments PK as driving table with correlated subqueries would be faster than GROUP BY on reaction_counts
asi.key_findings: For NoViewer (no reactions), this changes from 0 rows returned to 300 NULL rows, causing ~11% regression. For WithViewer, performance is same because both return ~300 rows. The GROUP BY on reaction_counts is actually more efficient when many comments have no reactions.
asi.next_action: Try caching reaction data or look for other attachReactions optimizations.
asi.rollback_reason: NoViewer cases regressed +11%; allocs up 15%. WithViewer unchanged. Not a net win.
